statement: Declaring an analysis tier on every pack rule (ADR-0016, cejel #414, 2026-10-06), the card's expected labels were wrong for nine of fifteen rules once matchers were read: D1, D4, D5 resolve imports across files with the type checker, and five LLM rules propagate taint through assignments and helpers (Python: a 12-pass interprocedural fixpoint) though no LLM file imports a parser. Importing a parser proves at least structural, never lexical. Rule: classify by what the matcher follows (names across files, data or control flow), cite the function, take the higher tier when ambiguous, and when the policy assertion then fails leave it red and report it rather than relabelling. Also check what a reachability guard actually reaches: the default-scan assertion was vacuous for the LLM pack, reachable only from a calibration entry.
